_note: Batch 4's three unconcluded tools, re-derived. Two of the three failures were MY scenario's fault, not the product's — the prompt was drawn from a synonym the prompt never actually contained, or named a job a sibling tool owns. The RUNBOOK's rule is that the prompt comes from the tool's OWN declared vocabulary; these do.

scenarios.prompt_source: _meta.synonyms['who is'] — its OWN phrase. The v1 prompt was 'What do we know about Mira Solene so far?', which contains memory_search's declared phrase 'what do we know about' and NOT this tool's longer 'what do we know about this character'. Longest-match therefore picked memory_search, correctly. That was a scenario defect, not a product one.

args.fact_text: Mira Solene is the last cartographer of the Obsidian Trench.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM glossary_entities WHERE book_id='{book_id}'
seed_assert.why: TWO characters, so an answer naming the right one is distinguishable from an answer that just echoes the only name present.

answer_expect.why: The seeded fact is the ONLY stored detail about her. A reply that does not carry it either did not read memory or read and dropped it; a reply carrying anything else about her is fabricated.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a read-intent turn changes the store, OR the reply invents biography beyond the single seeded fact, OR memory_recall_entity is not called on the turn. CONTROL: if memory_search is called instead and returns the same fact, this is a DECLARATION overlap finding, not a failure of this tool — record it as such rather than as a miss.

ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — an entity with no stored facts must say so, not invent.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — project-scoped; a second account must not recall these facts.

scenarios.prompt: Check the live inventory of my configured provider — which models does it actually offer right now?
scenarios.prompt_source: _meta.synonyms['inventory'] + ['models this provider offers']. The v1 prompt was 'What models can I use?', which is settings_list_models' job ('models', 'my models', 'list models') — the model was RIGHT to use it, so the v1 expect_tool was wrong.

answer_expect.why:
🔴 THIS EXPECTATION WAS RECALIBRATED 2026-08-23, BECAUSE THE FIX MADE THE OLD PHRASE LIE.

The original gate was none_of:['currently offer'], calibrated on the BROKEN population where that phrase only ever occurred as the false claim — 'here is what your configured providers currently offer', said over registry rows. It discriminated perfectly THEN: 9 of the 10 pre-fix replies contained it and the single reply that actually called settings_provider_inventory did not.

After the result-level `note` shipped, 4 of 5 replies still contain 'currently offer' — inside a CORRECT sentence: 'These are the models currently REGISTERED in your account. If you want the live, real-time inventory of what your providers are currently offering, let me know and I can check that for you.' The gate was red over the right answer. A phrase-level gate calibrated on the broken population marks the very distinction the fix introduces, because the fixed answer has to NAME the thing it is not, in order to disclaim it.

So the expectation now asserts the PROPOSITION rather than a symptom of its absence, and the separation was measured over both populations before it was adopted:

    'registered in your account'   pre-fix  0/10   (c3-close-raw.json, c3-run-raw.json)
                                   post-fix 5/5    (c3-note-raw.json)
    'currently offer'              pre-fix  9/10   post-fix 4/5 — no longer discriminating

D-LIVE-INVENTORY-ANSWERED-FROM-THE-REGISTRY IS FIXED and this is the evidence for it. What is still not satisfied is a DIFFERENT bar: settings_provider_inventory is called 0/5, so the model stops at a correct disclaimer and an OFFER to check live inventory instead of checking it. That is the tool-surfacing problem, and it is why this tool concludes `blocked` and not `proven`.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the reply lists REGISTERED models (settings_list_models' answer) while claiming to have read the provider's live inventory — those are different sets and conflating them is the defect. CONTROL: this tool REQUIRES provider_credential_id, which only settings_list_providers supplies, so a correct turn is a two-call chain; a turn that calls only settings_list_providers has not reached the tool under test.

ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a provider that is down must say so, not return an empty list as if it offered nothing.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — user-scoped; another account's credential must not be readable.

scenarios.prompt: Run a drift check on this chapter — did the prose actually deliver the beats it was supposed to?
scenarios.prompt_source: _meta.synonyms['drift check'] + ['beat realized']. The v1 prompt used 'check conformance', also declared, but the fixture carried no arc and no prose, so the tool had nothing to check.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM chapters WHERE book_id='{book_id}' AND coalesce(word_count,0) > 0
seed_assert.why: Conformance checks PROSE against a plan. Chapter bodies live in object storage (storage_key), so word_count is the column-level proxy for 'this chapter has prose'. With no prose the tool has nothing to run on and a refusal would be correct behaviour scored as a miss — which is what v1 measured.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the tool runs and reports conformance without any prose or arc actually existing (a check that cannot fail is not a check), OR a cost-gated tool spends LLM tokens without minting a confirm card. NOTE: this is Tier W and cost-gated, so the expected LIVE outcome is a CONFIRM CARD (ok=false, error=null, status=input_required), NOT a completed run — per dump-calls.sql that is a gated proposal, not a failure.

ship_audit.gate: The confirm card IS the audit here — an arc-scope run re-extracts and spends tokens, so an ungated run would be the defect.
ship_audit.empty_case: OWED — a chapter with no bound motifs/arc must refuse clearly rather than report vacuous conformance.
